lines.text: Thursday, November 12th, a little after 11 in the morning in New York. Somewhere inside Microsoft's cloud, servers start dropping out.
lines.say: Thursday, November twelfth, a little after eleven in the morning in New York. Somewhere inside Microsoft's cloud, servers start dropping out.

lines: Within about an hour, people in 74 countries were reporting that Outlook, Teams and other Microsoft services had stopped working.

lines.text: You couldn't send an email. You couldn't book, move or cancel a meeting.

lines: The next morning, before the stock market had even opened, Microsoft's shares were already falling.
It wasn't just email. Outlook, Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint and Copilot were all hit.
On the outage tracker Downdetector, reports for Outlook alone peaked at around 140,000.
At its worst, there were nearly 20,000 new reports every minute, compared with fewer than 15 on a normal Thursday.

lines.text: Microsoft said there was "elevated load across multiple regions". A number of servers became unexpectedly unavailable, which put more strain on the ones still running.
lines.say: Microsoft said there was elevated load across multiple regions. A number of servers became unexpectedly unavailable, which put more strain on the ones still running.

lines: Some servers were failing automated health checks. And when Microsoft brought them back, they could become unresponsive again as soon as traffic hit them.
Engineers patched a part of the system that handles sign-ins and routing traffic.
Microsoft said it saw no sign of a cyberattack. Australia's home affairs minister said Microsoft believed it was more like the 2024 CrowdStrike meltdown: an update gone wrong.
The real cause, Microsoft says, will come in its post-incident report.
In Japan, government ministries struggled to email each other.

lines.text: In Britain, the NHS told patients to keep their appointments, and some police forces asked people to use phone lines instead of online forms.
lines.say: In Britain, the N.H.S. told patients to keep their appointments, and some police forces asked people to use phone lines instead of online forms.

lines.text: The shipping giant Maersk and the stock-market operator Euronext reported problems. Luxury group Richemont's results were delayed, and Workhorse postponed its earnings.
lines.say: The shipping giant Mersk and the stock-market operator Euronext reported problems. Luxury group Reeshmont's results were delayed, and Workhorse postponed its earnings.

lines.text: Airlines in India rerouted customer emails. In the US, cities like Austin, Jacksonville and Baltimore County lost email; Austin said its 911 service was not affected.
lines.say: Airlines in India rerouted customer emails. In the U.S., cities like Austin, Jacksonville and Baltimore County lost email. Austin said its nine one one service was not affected.

lines: Even AI companies like OpenAI and Anthropic reported problems with tools that connect to Microsoft.

It really helps the channel.

lines.text: Early on Friday, Microsoft reported "early signs of stabilization", starting in Asia-Pacific.
lines.say: Early on Friday, Microsoft reported early signs of stabilization, starting in Asia-Pacific.

lines: To protect messages stuck in limbo, it extended the email retry window to 48 hours, so delayed emails wouldn't simply be lost.

lines.text: But later it admitted that one fix was "not working as expected", and gave no timeline for a full recovery.
lines.say: But later it admitted that one fix was not working as expected, and gave no timeline for a full recovery.

lines: At 9:30 a.m., the New York Stock Exchange opens. But trading starts earlier, in what's called pre-market.
On Friday morning, Microsoft's shares were down almost three percent before the bell, at around 508 dollars, while futures for the wider tech market barely moved.
For a company worth nearly four trillion dollars, a fall like that wipes out roughly 100 billion dollars of value, on paper.

lines.text: Microsoft is selling the world on AI and its cloud. On Thursday, that same cloud struggled to deliver an email.
One company's servers. Millions of inboxes. Governments, hospitals, airlines and markets, all waiting.

lines: This story is still developing, and we'll update you as it does.
This has been Toppled Giants.
